Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: The seven evaluated flood events generated approximately $4.0 billion in property damage across the North Carolina study area, of which 66% was uninsured; among affected mortgage borrowers, only 48% carried flood insurance; approximately 32% of flood-exposed borrowers lacked sufficient income or collateral to finance repairs through home-equity-based borrowing, facing credit constraints from negative equity, liquidity issues, or both, which placed their financial recovery at risk.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: Awareness-raising campaigns targeting citizens were found to be quite common across several developed countries, but insurer engagement in risk-reduction measures such as warning systems or land-use planning remained limited, since these are perceived as mainly governmental tasks; significant barriers included information gaps on the effectiveness of property-level protection measures and affordability requirements for risk-based pricing; the study proposes organized data collection on property-level protection measures and public-private partnerships where governments and insurers jointly insure high-risk properties at affordable premiums, concluding that actual insurer engagement falls considerably short of the theoretical potential for insurance to stimulate flood risk reduction.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: Without DRR interventions, global coastal flood expected annual damages are projected to exceed USD 1.3 trillion by 2080, directly affecting an estimated 11.5 million people annually; among individual measures, dykes and coastal levees achieved 98% efficacy at meeting risk targets (implementation cost USD 86 billion), compared to 49% for dry-proofing (USD 151 billion), 11% for zoning restrictions (USD 27 million), and just 6% for foreshore vegetation (USD 366 million); over 90% of sub-national regions worldwide could achieve their relative risk-constant targets if at least one of the investigated DRR measures were employed.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: The land-use model validated with 93.20% overall accuracy and a kappa coefficient of 0.89 against actual 2015 land use; built-up land was projected to increase about 6% by 2030 and 13% by 2050 relative to the 2015 baseline, with cropland losses of 723.59 to 876.97 km^2 depending on scenario; total flooded area expanded by 162.43 km^2 under RCP2.6 and 189.44 km^2 under RCP8.5 between 2030 and 2050; under the most severe scenario, about 4.68% and 5.96% of the total existing urban area in 2030 and 2050, respectively, would be susceptible to flood risk.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: A hydrograph recession exponent exceeding 2 reliably signals heavy-tailed flood behavior; median recession exponent values for heavy-tailed cases ranged from 2.64 to 2.92, compared to 1.84 to 2.0 for non-heavy-tailed cases, even when data was reduced to two-year periods; the proposed index showed distance correlation coefficients of 0.45, 0.44, and 0.81 with empirical power-law exponents for daily streamflows, ordinary peak flows, and monthly maxima respectively, demonstrating the index's stability and superior performance compared to conventional methods requiring longer records, across 386 case studies spanning seasonal categories.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: Among 212 surveyed residents of flood-prone Greater Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, mean scores (5-point scale) were 4.20 for flood preparedness, 4.16 for risk perception, and 3.97 for adaptive capacity; 87.3% of respondents showed high preparedness, 85.4% showed high risk awareness, and 66.5% showed high adaptive capacity; 87.3% had implemented property protection measures and 68.9% held flood insurance, while 66.5% reported moderate to complete quality-of-life disruption from flooding; Spearman correlations showed risk perception and adaptive capacity most strongly linked (rho=0.743, p<0.001), followed by preparedness-adaptive capacity (rho=0.453) and risk perception-preparedness (rho=0.485).

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: Tropical Cyclone Idai's March 2019 compound flooding in Mozambique caused an estimated USD 341 million in factual damage, flooding approximately 82,000 buildings across a 3,500 km^2 affected area, with 81% of damage concentrated in the Beira region; attribution modeling comparing factual to medium counterfactual scenarios found climate change increased flood volume by 5-19% (250-1000 million m^3), flood extent by 1-5% (40-170 km^2), and flood damage by 8-35% (USD 30-120 million); rainfall trends drove the largest volume/extent increases (5-19% and 1-4%) but smaller damage increases (2-8%), while wind and sea-level-rise trends drove the largest damage increase (6-27%) despite minimal effect on volume/extent (0.2-0.8% and 0.1-0.6%).

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: For the first event-based assessment of hurricane-driven flooding on a small island, combining synthetic hurricane rainfall from 4,909 modeled events (four climate models, HAPPI ensemble) with the LISFLOOD-FP hydrodynamic model at 20 m resolution across Puerto Rico's 9,100 km^2, approximately 8-10% of Puerto Rico's population currently faces flood exposure at the 5-year return period (2-5% at the 2-year return period); under 1.5 degC warming, this exposure is projected to increase by 2-15% at the 5-year return period, and under 2 degC warming by 1-20%; the model was validated against Hurricane Maria (2017) high-water-mark data, yielding RMSEs of 1.18-1.22 m, comparable to data-rich-region validations.

FloodQA_Question: Developing a coupled Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes model with two-phase water-air flow to simulate precipitation-induced karst-stream interactions, how does rainfall intensity affect recharge complexity across karst media, and why does matrix storage carry over between rain events while conduit storage does not?
Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: The coupled Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes two-phase (water-air) model of karst-stream interactions found that higher rainfall intensities produce more complex recharge processes, involving multi-media collaborative recharge and shifting discharge contribution ratios among epikarst, conduits, matrix, and streams; during consecutive rain events, groundwater stored in porous matrix media substantially influenced subsequent stream levels because of slow release, whereas conduit storage showed minimal carry-over effects due to rapid drainage; conduit geometry, epikarst permeability, and matrix porosity were found to differentially control discharge magnitude, timing, and distribution, information relevant to karst water resource and flood management.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: In a 356-household survey (217 in Lethem, 139 in Tabatinga, Guyana), the 27 May 2021 flood recorded 100.88 mm of total precipitation over seven days, while the 22 May 2022 flood recorded 190.52 mm over seven days, with flood depths exceeding 1 meter in vulnerable zones; the 2022 flood evacuated 100 persons and affected 500 people in Lethem; households reported flood damage costs of GYD 60,000-90,000 against average monthly incomes of GYD 100,000-200,000, with work disruption of 10-30 days per event, and farmers showed the least capacity to manage flood impacts; the study proposed a Flood Conveyance Solution (channels and embankments) for Tabatinga and a Water Storage and Bio-retention Solution (detention basins and drainage infrastructure) for Lethem.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: In 106 coupled 1D/2D InfoWorks ICM simulations of decentralized nature-based solutions for a flat 3.4 km^2 urban catchment in Berlin, Germany, intensive and retention green roofs achieved the greatest flood reduction for the 100-year rainfall event (48.9 mm), at 33.5-33.7%, with retention roofs fully detaining an extreme 100 mm event; infiltration systems designed for 100-year storms reduced flooding 12.2-33.7% (versus 6.1-21.6% for 5-year-designed systems) for the 100-year event, roughly three times more effective than 5-year systems under extreme rainfall; tree pits and trenches were far less effective (1.6-7.0% reduction); maximum water levels at the flooding center fell from 56 cm at baseline to 46 cm with 50% swale implementation and 28 cm with 100% implementation.

Source_Paper_Title: Flood frequency analysis using mean daily flows vs. instantaneous peak flows
Authors: Bartens, A.; Shehu, B.; Haberlandt, U.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: Across 648 German catchments (486 sites with at least 30-year records, 103 used for calibration over 1979-2012, record lengths 11-183 years), using mean daily flows instead of instantaneous peak flows can underestimate mean annual peak flow by up to 80%, with the error's magnitude primarily dependent on catchment area and gauge elevation; a proposed peak-to-volume ratio (p/V) correction model applied to L-moments of MDF maximum annual series reduced flood quantile errors by up to 60%, performing best for catchments under 500 km^2 but losing effectiveness below 100 km^2 and at gauge elevations under 100 m, with the MDF-IPF relationship also differing between summer and winter flood seasonality.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: For the June 2023 Braunschweig, Germany pluvial flood, caused by intense rainfall of 60 L/m^2 in a short time, the GPU-accelerated RIM2D hydrodynamic model simulated the 48-hour event 211 times faster than real time (58 minutes) at 10-meter resolution, 50 times faster (13 minutes) at 5-meter resolution, and 6.5 times faster on a single GPU at 2-meter resolution (75 million cells), with multi-GPU implementation further reducing runtimes to 7 and 29 minutes at 10 m and 5 m; the model produced maximum water depths exceeding 50 cm in central urban areas plus flow velocity, population, and building damage estimates, and was validated against 164 volunteered geographic information points from citizen photos and videos, showing strong alignment with observed flood extents and depths.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: Using buses as standardized height references in a dataset of 1,008 original social-media images (expanded to 2,184 via augmentation, with 1,562 annotated bus instances across four flood-risk levels), the recommended YOLOv8s model achieved mAP50 of 0.662 on the original dataset, improving to 0.734 after augmentation (mAP50-95 improving from 47.3% to 58.2%), representing gains exceeding 10% for mAP50 and 20% for mAP50-95; YOLOv8s outperformed YOLOv5s by 19.3% on the original data and offered the best balance of accuracy and computational efficiency, with substantially shorter training time than the larger YOLOv8l configuration.

Source_Paper_Title: Atmospheric Rivers Feeding Terrestrial Floods in the Senyar 2025 Event: A Conceptual Review

FloodQA_Question: Reviewing the atmospheric-river-fed terrestrial floods associated with the Senyar event across Aceh, North Sumatra, and West Sumatra, Indonesia, what death toll, displacement, and peak daily rainfall totals were recorded across the affected provinces, and how did integrated vapor transport change between offshore and coastal locations?
Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: The atmospheric-river-fed Senyar flooding event across Aceh, North Sumatra, and West Sumatra, Indonesia caused over 1,200 deaths, displaced approximately 80,000 people, and destroyed nearly 650 bridges; record daily rainfall reached 311 mm in Aceh, 262 mm in Medan, 230 mm in Tapanuli, and 154 mm in West Sumatra; Integrated Vapor Transport (IVT) exceeded 500 kg/m/s offshore but dropped below 270 kg/m/s at the coastline, with wind speed reducing by about 50% within 50-100 km before landfall; the review's core hypothesis is that vegetation-induced surface roughness slows onshore winds, causing moisture congestion that generates precipitation before reaching the mountains, a mechanism made more consequential by West Sumatra's lowland population share rising from 9% in 1830 to 49% in 1990.

Source_Paper_Title: Compound Flood Risk Assessment of Extreme Rainfall and High River Water Level

FloodQA_Question: Using copula functions to build joint probability distributions of rainfall and river water level for Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province, China (2005-2022 data) with InfoWorks ICM hydrodynamic simulation, how did flooded area change when a 50-year-return-period high river water level was added to baseline rainfall-only scenarios?
Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: For Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province, China, using copula-based joint probability distributions of rainfall and river water level (2005-2022 data) combined with InfoWorks ICM hydrodynamic modeling, flooded area under baseline rainfall-only scenarios ranged from 0.67% to 5.39% of the study area, but rose to 8.98-12.80% when a 50-year-return-period high river water level was combined with rainfall; the joint risk probability of combined rainfall and high water levels was significantly higher than considering either factor separately, and high river water levels were found to play a critical role in increasing both flood extent and depth, especially when even low rainfall coincided with elevated water levels.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: The physics-guided PHY-FTMA-LSTM model, trained on 20 flood events and validated on 10 events spanning 1964-2017 for the 17,100 km^2 Luan River basin (Sandaohezi station), achieved a Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.988 at 1-hour lead time and 0.908 at 6-hour lead time; compared to a baseline LSTM, NSE improved from 0.977 to 0.988 at the 1-hour lead time, while RMSE decreased by 27.4% and MAE decreased by 49.6%, with the model integrating runoff, rainfall, evapotranspiration, and initial soil moisture under monotonic physical constraints enforcing hydrological principles.

Source_Paper_Title: The 2024 cascading glacial lake outburst flood in the Thame Valley of Everest region, Nepal: process, impacts and implications

FloodQA_Question: Investigating the 2024 cascading glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) in the Thame Valley, Everest region, Nepal, what combined water volume and peak discharge were released, how quickly did the flood reach Thame Village, and what economic losses and displacement resulted despite no fatalities?
Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: The 2024 cascading glacial lake outburst flood in Nepal's Thame Valley, Everest region, released a combined water volume of approximately 7.7x10^5 m^3 with peak discharge exceeding 800 m^3/s, reaching Thame Village in about 22 minutes with maximum flow heights of 4 meters; the upper lake had expanded to 0.11 km^2 before outburst while the lower lake grew 20% between 1989-2024, and post-event the upper lake level dropped about 4.6 m and the lower lake about 12 m; flood effects were traced 50 km downstream, causing an estimated USD 6.18 million in losses and displacing 135 people within Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality, with no fatalities reported; the event was preceded by a 14-day wet period and temperatures exceeding the 90th-95th percentile, against a regional warming trend of 0.017 degC/year since 1990.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: For a simultaneous probable-maximum-flood dam-failure scenario at the Dongpu and Dafangying reservoirs in Hefei, China, integrating MIKE FLOOD 1D/2D hydrodynamic modeling with a five-indicator (inundation depth, arrival time, inundation duration, population density, road network density) AHP-entropy-weighted fuzzy comprehensive evaluation substantially reduced the extent of identified high-risk areas and altered their spatial distribution compared to a hazard-only assessment; flood arrival time and population density emerged as the most influential risk factors, with high-risk zones concentrated along upstream channels where high-velocity floodwaters coincide with dense population and economic activity.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: Assessing levee breach risk at five representative sites along a 153.7 km reach of the Daling River, China under 50-, 100-, and 200-year return period flood scenarios using a coupled 1D-2D hydrodynamic and multi-indicator framework, the Lituocun site ranked highest for composite risk, followed by Shenglitun, Youxicun, Yangguicun, and Xiangyangzha; the study found that as return periods increased, the growth in direct economic losses consistently outpaced the expansion of inundation area, revealing a nonlinear 'amplification effect' in disaster consequences under extreme exceedance conditions not captured by existing levee safety assessments.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: The 3D numerical model, coupling RANS hydrodynamics with a volume-of-fluid method, sediment erosion, and breach evolution modules, predicted breach flow rates and depths with relative errors under 5% for both peak discharge and time-to-peak compared to experimental observations; among 245 documented landslide dam failures, over 90% resulted from overtopping; the real-world 2018 Baige landslide dam breach on China's Jinsha River, used as a validation case, produced two breach events affecting over 100,000 people with peak discharge reaching 31,000 m^3/s.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: Following Hurricane Irma, analysis of cell-phone location data combined with hydrodynamic flood modeling for Collier and Monroe Counties, Florida found 123 uninhabitable buildings among 1,067 analyzed locations; Monroe County showed 13.5% of analyzed users displaced by uninhabitability versus 6.0% in Collier County; maximum unit discharge was found to be generally the best predictor of habitability, outperforming depth, velocity, and wave height individually; wooden structure habitability was significantly influenced by hazard level, whereas concrete structure habitability was not, revealing a stark construction-type vulnerability gap.

Source_Paper_Title: Modeling regional production capacity loss rates considering response bias: insights from a questionnaire survey on the Zhengzhou flood

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: In a 424-enterprise survey conducted April-May 2023 covering manufacturing (148), accommodation/catering (68), wholesale/retail trade (137), and other sectors (71) affected by the Zhengzhou, China flood, the sector suffering the highest production capacity loss rate shifts at an inundation depth threshold of 80 cm: below 80 cm the wholesale and retail trade sector suffers the highest loss rate, while above 80 cm the manufacturing sector becomes the greater concern; production capacity losses reach approximately 20% even without direct inundation, attributable to indirect supply-chain, workforce, and infrastructure disruptions; Monte Carlo simulation-based prediction intervals narrowed at greater depths, improving predictability for emergency planning.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: The INSYDE-content model, validated against the 2002 Lodi flood (194 buildings, 3.1 million euros in losses) and the 2010 Caldogno flood (169 buildings, 3.1 million euros in losses) in Italy, found content damage may represent up to 50% of total building damage, with content-to-building damage ratios ranging 0.26-0.42 depending on inundation duration; mean absolute errors were 14,185-16,962 euros per building; sensitivity analysis ranked inundation depth as the primary driver of damage-estimate uncertainty (median uncertainty 4,500-6,800 euros), followed by building type (3,000-3,500 euros) and ground floor level (1,500-2,900 euros); the model covers 11 standard household item categories including beds, sofas, wardrobes, and appliances.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: For the Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna basin and Bangladesh delta over 1988-2021 (31 years, excluding 1996-1998), basin-wide monsoon precipitation averaged 1,158 mm (range 941-1,326 mm) and mean seasonal flood area was 32,515 km^2 (range 11,423-48,534 km^2); Gumbel copula analysis revealed significant upper-tail dependence (lambda_u = 0.227) between precipitation and flood extent; saturated antecedent root-zone soil moisture conditions multiplied extreme flood probability by 1.16x relative to median conditions, with probability of extreme flooding rising from 11.10% under dry conditions to 16.82% under normal conditions to 19.49% under saturated conditions; for a 1-in-20-year event, the joint OR return period was about 11.51 years versus an AND return period of about 76.40 years.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: Integrating HEC-RAS hydraulic modeling with GIS across three northeastern Thailand basins (Lam Saphung 743.74 km^2, Phrom River 2,264.66 km^2, Chern River Part 1 1,899.65 km^2), model performance ranged R^2 0.745-0.994 and Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency 0.653-0.893; comparing 2006 to 2019 land use and hydrological conditions, flood-prone areas increased by up to 5.49% in the Phrom basin and up to 5.50% in the Chern basin; flood depths exceeded 1.5 meters in certain regions, with high-risk zones covering up to 105.2 km^2 during severe events.

Source_Paper_Title: Mitigating the impact of increased drought-flood abrupt alternation events under climate change: the role of reservoirs in the Lancang-Mekong River Basin

FloodQA_Question: Using the THREW hydrological model with a reservoir operations module for 122 reservoirs and 5 CMIP6 climate models to study drought-flood abrupt alternation (DFAA) in the Lancang-Mekong River Basin, which alternation type dominates future projections, and how effective are reservoirs at mitigating drought-to-flood versus flood-to-drought risks?
Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: Using the THREW hydrological model coupled with a reservoir operations module for 122 reservoirs and five CMIP6 GCMs, drought-to-flood (DTF) abrupt alternation events were found to dominate the Lancang-Mekong River Basin, exceeding flood-to-drought (FTD) event probabilities at all intensity levels, with mild-intensity events representing 58-90% of DTF and 75-100% of FTD occurrences, and DTF probability increasing more sharply than FTD probability in future projections; reservoirs substantially reduced DTF risks in both wet and dry seasons and significantly shortened monthly DFAA duration, but their effectiveness against FTD risks, particularly in dry seasons, was comparatively weaker, with a positive correlation found between a reservoir's total storage capacity and its overall DFAA mitigation ability.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: Storm Daniel's flooding of the Thessalian plain, central Greece (3-8 September 2023), mapped using the SAR-based RAPID inundation system combined with CORINE land cover and crop maps, inundated a total of 1,150 km^2, of which approximately 820 km^2 (70%) was agricultural land; cotton crop damage exceeded 282 km^2, representing about 30% of the total area planted with cotton in central Greece; wheat impacts totaled 57.5 km^2 of durum wheat and 55 km^2 of other wheat inundated; livestock impacts included more than 14,000 poultry/ornithoids and 21,500 sheep and goats affected.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: In a fuzzy-entropy TOPSIS assessment of typhoon resilience across 27 Chinese cities in seven major river basins (2020-2022), the Haihe, Liaohe, and Yangtze River basins ranked highest in resilience while the Pearl River basin performed weakest; Shanghai achieved the highest individual resilience score (0.5907), followed by Yantai (0.4087), with Haikou and Beijing close behind; China experienced CNY 47.49 billion in typhoon-related losses in 2023, about 13.8% of total disaster-related economic damage that year; the analysis found that the direction of regional economic investment, especially government fiscal spending, mattered more for resilience than raw economic development level.

Ground_Truth_Answer_Summary: Across 11 years (2011-2021) of natural hazard disturbances on the German rail network, heavy-rainfall events increased the odds of flood events by a factor of 22.7, with about 23% of flood events occurring after a heavy-rainfall trigger; heavy rainfall increased tree-fall event odds by a smaller factor of 3.62, with only 2% of tree-fall events following such a trigger; gravitational mass movements showed no statistically significant rainfall effect despite 14% showing a temporal connection; the heavy-rainfall index and 21-day antecedent precipitation index were identified as the rainfall characteristics with the strongest impact on hazard occurrence.
